title: Managing Power, Performance and Reliability in the Chiplet Era - Semiwiki
gist: An Amkor/proteanTecs webinar argues chiplet-era packages require replacing binary pass/fail test with on-chip telemetry 'deep data', shift-left Known Good Die screening, cross-stage correlation and lifetime in-field monitoring to raise compound yield and reliability.

insights.claim: Advanced 2.5D/3D packages mixing dies from different processes, high-speed die-to-die interfaces and extreme power and thermal stress severely reduce internal visibility into hardware behavior.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Creates demand for new test, telemetry and DFT solutions in AI accelerators.

insights.claim: Finding a hardware defect gets exponentially more expensive the further a device moves down the production line, so detecting flaws only after final assembly wastes time and money.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Early screening has outsized ROI in expensive multi-die AI packages.
insights.quote: finding a hardware defect gets exponentially more expensive the further a device moves down the production line

insights.claim: Larger die and package sizes mean longer test times and higher test costs.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Rising test intensity benefits test equipment and OSAT test services.

insights.claim: Die-to-die interconnects often run at data rates far beyond what package-level tester interfaces can handle, making their actual behavior hard to map.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Test access gap drives adoption of on-chip monitors and new DFT methods.

insights.claim: Traditional pass/fail testing cannot catch subtle signs of marginal performance or latent defects.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Binary testing is insufficient for AI-scale reliability requirements.
insights.quote: Traditional pass/fail testing cannot catch subtle signs of marginal performance or latent defects.

insights.claim: Test access in multi-die systems relies on die-to-die standards and interfaces like UCIe, PCIe, CXL and NVLink combined with advanced DFX, streaming scan networks and expanded test bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Interconnect standards are becoming test infrastructure, not just data paths.

insights.claim: proteanTecs embeds monitoring agents and sensors on-chip to capture high-fidelity parametric 'deep data' during production and mission-mode operation, which software analytics turn into actionable intelligence.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: On-chip telemetry IP is an emerging layer in the chiplet value chain.

insights.claim: By combining parametric data such as IDDQ currents and timing behavior with process signatures and machine-learning models, proteanTecs flags die-level outliers that pass regular test limits.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: ML-based outlier screening can lift compound yield in costly packages.

insights.claim: Catching marginal dies during wafer sort enables smarter Known Good Die selection, directly boosting final compound yields for multi-die packages.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Compound yield improvements directly lower cost for AI accelerator packages.

insights.claim: Correlating device behavior across wafer sort, assembly, final test and system-level evaluation creates a Measure-Correlate-Identify-Improve feedback loop that isolates failure root causes.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Cross-stage data unification is a software opportunity in test.

insights.claim: proteanTecs monitors timing margins and internal telemetry on deployed hardware to support real-time degradation tracking, predictive failure alerts and remaining-useful-life calculations.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: In-field monitoring could reduce costly AI cluster downtime.

insights.claim: The industry must stop viewing testing as isolated checkups and track hardware behavior across its entire operational lifespan.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Opens recurring lifecycle-analytics revenue models in semiconductors.

insights.claim: As chiplet architectures become the backbone for AI workloads, seeing inside a package is becoming as critical as the ability to manufacture it, and telemetry data becomes a competitive asset.
insights.speaker: Kalar Rajendiran
insights.so_what: Observability vendors may capture rising value as AI hardware complexity grows.
insights.quote: peering inside a package is becoming just as critical as the physical ability to manufacture it
